original.title: Campus Life
original.lede: All students live on board. The Office of the Dean (Students’ Welfare) is responsible for residential life, student activities and wellbeing.

pirate.title: Life on Board

original.heading: About Us
paragraphs: The Office of the Dean (Students’ Welfare) is responsible for all aspects of student life outside the classroom, including accommodation, clubs, sport, cultural activities and wellbeing.
The Office coordinates 42 student clubs and 9 hostels, the annual programme of festivals, and access to counselling and mental health services.

pirate.heading: The Dean of Students’ Welfare
pirate.kicker: The office that answers the question “who do I ask about this?”
paragraphs: The Dean of Students’ Welfare looks after everything that happens outside lectures: hammocks, clubs, sport, festivals and wellbeing.
There are 42 clubs and 9 hostels on board, and a counselling service for when the sea feels rough. All of it runs through this office.

aside.label: Good to know
aside.text: Mental health and wellness support is part of this office. Asking for help is completely normal on this ship.

original.heading: Vision
paragraphs: To provide a safe, inclusive and supportive residential environment in which every student can develop academically, personally and socially.
To ensure that every student has access to the resources, mentorship and opportunities required to reach their full potential.

pirate.heading: What the office is aiming for
paragraphs: A safe, friendly ship where every student grows, in class and out of it.
Everyone gets the help, mentors and chances they need to do their best. Nobody gets left on the dock.

original.heading: Objectives
items: To promote the all-round development of students.
To encourage self-discipline, responsibility and mutual respect.
To administer scholarships and financial support schemes.
To maintain safe and comfortable hostel accommodation.
To support student clubs and societies.
To organise cultural, sporting and technical events.
To maintain a clean and sustainable campus.

pirate.heading: Seven promises, in plain English
items: Help every student grow, in every way.
A culture of self-discipline, responsibility and respect.
Make sure scholarships and support actually reach the students they are meant for.
Hostels that are safe, comfortable and feel like home. Hammocks included.
Back every student club, from robotics to knot-tying.
Plenty of cultural, sports and technical events, so everyone finds a talent beyond the classroom.
Keep the ship clean. The sea is watching.

pirate.heading: The Map Room
pirate.tagline: Officially the Central Library. Every map on board is kept here, and these are the people who know where.

original.heading: Geological Museum
paragraphs: The Geological Museum, established in 1717, holds 4,018 exhibits, including minerals, rocks, fossils and models of geological processes.
Exhibits are arranged in three sections: Minerals and Crystals; Rocks and Structures; and Fossils and Landforms.
The collection has been assembled over three centuries by faculty, students and passing ships.
Approximately half of the collection is on public display. The remainder is held in storage for research.

pirate.heading: The rock collection
pirate.kicker: Founded in 1717, the same year as the ship. Several exhibits are slightly older.
paragraphs: Davy Jones’ Rock Collection, our geological museum, has 4,018 exhibits: minerals, rocks, fossils and models of how the Earth works.
They are sorted into three sections: minerals and crystals; rocks and structures; fossils and landforms.
It took three centuries to collect them. Some were found by professors, some by students, and some simply landed on the deck.
About half are on display. The rest are in storage, being studied, or under a hammock somewhere.

aside.label: Visitor tip
aside.text: Start with the minerals and crystals. The rocks will still be there; that is rather the point of rocks.
